newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up on buying by support fund.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up on buying by support fund.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to rise on Thursday on continued buying by the newly-launched market support fund and on expectations that the country's exports would improve, brokers said.

"The market support fund is expected to continue buying like yesterday and this will boost the sentiment to a certain level. Local retail investors are anticipated to follow the fund on buying," said Suppachai Ekkul of Nithipat Capital.
The SET index, which dropped to eight-year lows last week, rose 19.09 points to 596.19 on brisk 6.3 billion baht turnover on Wednesday. The SET-50 index gained 1.73 points to 43.87.

Brokers said Krung Thai Bank Plc, the administrator of a 50 billion baht market support fund pooled in by commercial banks to help shore up the market, injected about one billion baht for the first time on Wednesday.
Krung Thai Bank declined to confirm that the support fund started buying on Wednesday but said it could begin tapping the fund from yesterday.
Brokers said comments by Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond earlier this week on an increase in exports in March would further boost the market sentiment.
